hook: Suspended compute costs $0 on Neon; PlanetScale's smallest HA Postgres cluster has a $15 monthly compute charge even when idle. Keep 0.25 CU awake on Neon Launch: 0.25 CU × 730 h = 182.5 CU-hours × $0.106 = $19.35/month before storage, versus $15/month for PlanetScale PS-5 HA.

sections.title: PlanetScale rents you a machine; Neon bills the hours it is awake
sections.content:
For Postgres with idle periods or many branches, compare billed CU-hours with dedicated clusters; existing Vitess-based MySQL still has an engine constraint.

> PlanetScale: capacity is a cluster you rent. Neon: compute is CU-hours, meaning compute size × hours running on Lakebase Postgres.

- PlanetScale charges for idle cluster capacity; storage, backups and egress can add charges. Each branch runs on its own separately billed dedicated cluster.
- Neon's paid plans charge for CU-hours used, while suspended compute costs $0. Its pricing describes Lakebase Postgres as “from Databricks”.

PlanetScale's docs say it plainly: there is no free plan.

> Figures below are AWS us-east-1 list prices checked 10 November 2026, or arithmetic on them; nothing is benchmarked.

sections.title: The $0 database out-bills the $15 cluster once it never sleeps
sections.content:
The bottom of each price list:

| Entry | Monthly | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| Neon Free | $0 | 100 CU-hours, 1 GB storage per project |
| PlanetScale PS-5, single node | $5 | 1/16 vCPU, 512 MiB |
| PlanetScale PS-5 HA | $15 | 1 primary + 2 replicas |

Now keep a 0.25 CU Neon compute awake all month on Launch: 0.25 × 730 h = 182.5 CU-hours × $0.106 = $19.35, before storage.

> Compute only: $19.35 − $15 = $4.35 more than PlanetScale's three-node cluster; capacity is not equivalent.

```python
# Awake hours/month before 0.25 CU on Neon Launch out-bills PS-5 HA.
CU, RATE, PS5_HA = 0.25, 0.106, 15.00
break_even = PS5_HA / (CU * RATE)
print(f"approximately {break_even:.2f} of 730 hours")
# Assumes 0.25 CU runs throughout the awake hours.
```

sections.title: Who should NOT pick Neon: existing Vitess-based MySQL deployments
sections.content:
Now one CU, awake all month:

| Option | Compute formula | Monthly |
|---|---|---|
| Neon Launch, 1 CU | 1 × 730 × $0.106 | $77.38 |
| Neon Scale, 1 CU | 1 × 730 × $0.222 | $162.06 |
| PlanetScale PS-80 HA | fixed cluster, arm64 | $148 |

Not identical machines. A CU is about 4 GB RAM; PS-80 is listed at 1 vCPU and 8 GiB plus two replicas.

- Scale's compute crossover: $148 ÷ (1 CU × $0.222/CU-hour) ≈ 666.67 h; choose PS-80 only if its capacity suits the workload.
- Neon's own typical-cost rows answer "how many hours?": intermittent load (140 CU-hours + 1 GB) is $15 on Launch, high load (3,000 CU-hours + 100 GB) is $353 on Launch and $701 on Scale.
- PlanetScale's SKU ladder answers "which size?", from PS-5 at $15 to PS-2560 at $4,529 HA on arm64.

> Do not pick Neon if you must retain Vitess-based MySQL; Launch also lacks an uptime SLA. Compare billed CU-hours with the cluster charge before attributing savings to suspension.

sections.title: Who should NOT pick PlanetScale: projects with a $0 budget
sections.content:
On PlanetScale every branch runs on its own dedicated cluster, billed separately and prorated to the millisecond. On Neon Launch a branch is a line item: 10 per project included, then $1.50 per branch-month, prorated hourly.

| 20 branches alive all month | Formula | Component/month |
|---|---|---|
| Neon Launch | 10 included + 10 × $1.50 | $15 extra-branch fees |
| PlanetScale, PS-5 HA each | 20 × $15 | $300 cluster compute |

- Add running compute and data storage on Neon; add storage, backups and transfer on PlanetScale.
- Millisecond proration helps PlanetScale with short-lived branches: one PS-5 HA branch costs $15 ÷ 730 h ≈ $0.02 per hour.
- Use actual branch lifetimes. Launch suspension after five minutes can be disabled.

Do not pick PlanetScale for a $0 budget; every database requires a paid subscription.

sections.title: Neki adds sharded Postgres, but its preview excludes production
sections.content:
Neki is PlanetScale's sharded Postgres, in platform preview since 10 September 2026. PlanetScale says preview is not for production, and that "some of those changes will be breaking".

> Apps reach it through a Neki router over the Postgres wire protocol.

- No single-node configuration: the smallest arm64 shard is PS-10 at $30, 1 primary and 2 replicas across 3 availability zones.
- Routers start at $6 (NKR-0). Production router compute = router rate × observed routers ÷ 3; the rate covers the three-router baseline, one per AZ.
- Four PS-20 shards plus NKR-20 routers: 4 × $50 + $170 × 3 ÷ 3 = $370/month, before storage, backups and network usage.

sections.title: Pick from measured compute, branch and data charges
sections.content:
Choose Neon when measured CU-hours plus branch, storage and transfer charges beat PlanetScale's total. Choose PlanetScale for suitable always-on cluster compute or an existing Vitess-shaped MySQL estate.

Check this today:

1. Pull last month's awake hours per Neon compute. For compute only: $15 ÷ (0.25 CU × $0.106/CU-hour) ≈ 566.04 h on Launch.
2. Count branches alive at once and how long each lives, and price them as PlanetScale clusters before copying the habit.
3. Check suspension configuration and billed CU-hours; add storage, backups and transfer before choosing.
4. Do not run production workloads on Neki's platform preview; evaluate it only outside production.

decision_matrix.situation: Dev and test databases idle overnight, one branch per pull request
decision_matrix.why: Suspended compute bills $0 and branches past the included 10 cost $1.50 per branch-month instead of a cluster each. Running compute, data storage and transfer remain separate.

decision_matrix.situation: Always-on database comparing compute charges only
decision_matrix.why: For compute only, 0.25 CU × 730 h = 182.5 CU-hours × $0.106 = $19.35 on Neon Launch, versus $15 for PlanetScale PS-5 HA; storage and other charges remain separate, and capacity must suit the workload.
Neon's pricing lists only Lakebase Postgres, so leaving Vitess would be an engine migration, not a vendor switch.

decision_matrix.situation: Side project or prototype with a $0 budget
decision_matrix.why: PlanetScale has no free plan, while Neon Free is permanent, needs no card and includes 100 CU-hours per project.
Neki is a platform preview and PlanetScale says not to run production on it.

decision_matrix.situation: Compliance-bound production (HIPAA BAA, uptime SLA) with traffic that idles for hours
decision_matrix.why: Scale includes self-serve HIPAA with a BAA and an SLA; suspended compute costs $0, while running compute costs $0.222/CU-hour. Suspension is configurable from 1 minute to always on.

decision_matrix.situation: Comparing one always-on Neon Scale CU with PS-80 HA compute prices
decision_matrix.pick: PlanetScale PS-80 HA, only if its capacity suits the workload
decision_matrix.why: Compute charges cross at $148 ÷ (1 CU × $0.222/CU-hour) ≈ 666.67 h; this compares prices, not equivalent workload capacity.

decision_matrix.situation: Need Launch's compute ceiling exceeded by a fixed-size deployment
decision_matrix.why: Launch autoscaling stops at 16 CU, while Scale offers fixed sizes up to 56 CU (224 GB RAM).

cost_math.label: Always-on small database, Neon Launch vs PlanetScale PS-5 HA
cost_math.formula: Neon Launch: 0.25 CU × 730 h = 182.5 CU-hours × $0.106/CU-hour = $19.35/month; PlanetScale PS-5 HA: $15/month cluster compute
cost_math.result: $19.35/month vs $15/month, compute only; different capacity, with storage and other charges separate

cost_math.label: One CU all month, Neon Launch / Neon Scale vs PlanetScale PS-80 HA (arm64)
cost_math.formula: Neon Launch: 1 CU × 730 h = 730 CU-hours × $0.106/CU-hour = $77.38; Neon Scale: 730 CU-hours × $0.222/CU-hour = $162.06; PlanetScale PS-80 HA arm64: $148/month
cost_math.result: Compute only: Launch $77.38; Scale $162.06; PS-80 $148/month. Not equivalent capacity; use PS-80 only if it suits the workload.

cost_math.label: 20 branches alive all month
cost_math.formula: Neon Launch: 20 branches = 10 included + 10 × $1.50 = $15/month extra-branch fees; PlanetScale: 20 × $15 = $300/month (PS-5 HA each), prorated to the millisecond
cost_math.result: Neon: $15 extra-branch fees plus running compute and data storage; PlanetScale: $300 cluster compute plus storage, backups and transfer. Not total bills.

cost_math.label: Neki platform preview — not production: four PS-20 shards plus routers
cost_math.formula: Neki is a platform preview, not production. Shards: 4 × $50 = $200; production router compute = router rate × observed routers ÷ 3 = $170 (NKR-20) × 3 ÷ 3 = $170; $200 + $170 = $370/month
cost_math.result: Neki is a platform preview, not production. $370/month before storage, backups and network usage.

verdict_summary: Pick Neon if your databases sleep: suspended compute costs $0, and a branch per pull request costs $1.50 a month instead of a cluster. Pick PlanetScale if production must stay awake on a fixed cluster charge, or you already run Vitess-shaped MySQL — and test Neki outside production only, because its preview excludes it.

faqs.q: Does Neon Launch come with an uptime SLA?
faqs.a: No; Launch has no SLA. The uptime SLA, HIPAA with a BAA, SOC 2 and ISO 27001/27701 arrive with Scale, along with private networking at $0.01/GB.

faqs.q: What does 100 GB of storage cost?
faqs.a: On Neon Launch it is 100 × $0.35 = $35/month. PlanetScale includes 10 GB per instance and bills the rest at a region volume rate it publishes only through an endpoint, on the primary and both replicas of an HA cluster.

Neon Launch includes 500 GB per project, then $0.10/GB. PlanetScale includes 100 GB/month on a production branch and 10 GB on development branches and PS-5 non-HA, then a region rate it does not print; ingress is free. At 1,024 GB on Neon Launch: 1,024 − 500 = 524 GB × $0.10 = $52.40/month; PlanetScale's overage rate is region-dependent and not printed.

faqs.q: When do PlanetScale backups add charges?
faqs.a: PlanetScale runs automated backups every 12 hours and includes backup and WAL storage up to twice disk size; overage costs $0.023 per GB-month on compressed size.
